The orchestrator and the provisioner also use separate credentials, which expire independently. Probe each against the provider’s account endpoint. Details are infrastructure — see rtj
comparing link_sha across hosts it is a real SHA on the load_all dispatcher and NA on every pak-installed cypher, so it can only ever fail. Key on repo_sha, read on each host from the checkout it installed from. fresh_sha was excluded alongside it on the grounds that it was NA everywhere and could only ever pass — that half was measured false on 2026-09-01 and the field is a real key since link#264
max(last_analyze) for vintage NULL on all ten primitives, measured. Empty in bash reads as “nothing to see”. Use GREATEST(last_analyze, last_autoanalyze), and since link#265 only as context beside the load stamp

The prep sentinel

cypher_prep.sh ends with a bare === READY, and the umbrella greps it anchored (grep -qx). Do not revert this to snapshot_bcfp.sh: complete, which was wrong in both directions: the snapshot emits it before lnk_persist_init runs, so a persist_init FATAL passed the gate and WSGs ran against a half-prepped cypher; and the snapshot’s legitimate skip-if-current path never emits it at all, so a skipped load read as FATAL. The -x anchor is what stops === READY (install stage only; ...) satisfying a full-prep check.

Two post-conditions, and why they are not optional

schema_consolidate DELETEs the destination bucket from every persist table (its step 3.5) and then COPYs (step 4). A host that produced nothing therefore does not merely fail to add rows — it removes the rows already there for those WSGs and returns ok = TRUE. (The log tables are left out of that DELETE, so a group’s log history survives it; link#354.) So:

  • before consolidate, every host must account for its whole bucket, read from its database: <schema>.log rows for the run_uid with date_end set, plus SKIP markers from the log, which write no row (link#347);
  • after consolidate, every run WSG must have rows in <persist>.streams from a build this run finished.

The second is detection rather than prevention, and it is the one that would have caught link#246 on day one regardless of cause.

A missing group costs only itself (link#348)

The coverage check used to exit 1 on the first run group with no rows, before the recompute. One failed group then left every other group’s access computed against an incomplete barrier set, with no recompute rows at all. It also asked only whether rows existed, so a failed group holding an earlier run’s rows passed and was recomputed as this run’s.

Now run_coverage (data-raw/study_area_finish.sh) splits the run’s groups (every bucket, less SKIPs) into five classes, read on the dispatcher after consolidate:

class rows in streams finished this run what happens
recompute yes yes recomputed and compared
no rows no no named at the end
earlier or partial yes no named; its rows are left as they are
lost at consolidate no yes named
not consolidated any any named; its host’s consolidate failed (below)

“Finished this run” means the group’s newest <schema>.log row (max date_start, the rule schema_consolidate.R uses for which build a group’s persist rows hold) is the run_uid’s and has date_end set. Consolidate copies a group’s log rows home (link#354), and the driver adds the dispatcher’s done markers and each cypher’s consolidated bucket. A failed build leaves its row open (.lnk_log_run_fail sets only notes), and its pre-persist can leave streams rows, so rows alone do not make a group “this run’s”. “Newest” matters for a --recompute-only days later: a group a later run rebuilt, or a hand re-run under the same uid that failed after its pre-persist, has a closed row for the uid that no longer names its rows. The classes are written to <TS>_coverage.tsv, beside the compare CSV, which covers the first class only. The recompute and the compare run over the first class only. If that class is empty, neither runs and the report says why. Any other class makes the run exit non-zero, and the report names the groups and the recovery:

PGOPTIONS='-c statement_timeout=<the run bound, e.g. 30min>' \
LNK_RUN_UID=<uid> [LNK_RUN_LABEL=<label>] LNK_SCHEMA=<schema> \
  LNK_GUARD_DOWNSTREAM=warn LNK_HABITAT_GATE=0 LNK_LOAD=loadall \
  Rscript data-raw/wsg_run_one.R <WSG> <config>          # each missing group
bash data-raw/study_area_run.sh --recompute-only --run-uid=<uid> \
  --config=<config> --schema=<schema> [--run-label=<label>] [--wsgs=<the run's groups>]

--recompute-only runs the driver’s tail and nothing else: no droplet, no pre-flight, no consolidate. It recomputes every group of the run, not just the re-modelled ones, because a re-modelled group’s barriers change access upstream of it. Without --wsgs=, the expected set is the groups the run recorded in <TS>_run_wsgs.tsv (wsg, host, skip, run_uid; a run_uid’s prefix is its TS), together with any group holding a log row for the run_uid on the dispatcher (link#358). The driver writes that file as soon as the buckets resolve, before any spend, and rewrites it after the per-host accounting with each host’s SKIPs, so a group that failed on a cloud host, or before its first log row, is still named. A run from before #358 has no file and falls back to the log alone, where such a group has no row and only --wsgs= gets it named. A file that names another run_uid stops a bare --recompute-only. A --wsgs= that leaves out the run’s groups warns. It refuses a --config other than the one the run’s log rows name, since a forgotten --config would recompute every group under bcfishpass and stamp the rows with the run’s uid. It skips the discharge resolution as well as the pre-flight, but still checks for fresh.streams_vw_bcfp, which the compare reads.

It also cannot rescue a group whose build finished but whose date_end UPDATE failed (.lnk_log_run_finish is soft). A full run counts that group through its done marker, but --recompute-only has only the log, so it reports the group as “earlier or partial” every time. Re-model it. A missing group in a kept host’s bucket is listed apart in the report, which defers to kept_hosts.tsv: settle it there first (consolidate only groups where groups_measured is yes, never groups_partial), and re-model only what is still missing. --recompute-only warns when a kept_hosts.tsv names the run_uid.

A consolidate that refuses one source does not stop the run (link#358). schema_consolidate loops past a source it refuses (dest_log_newer, which one group can trigger, and the other checks made before anything is deleted) or fails on mid-copy, so the other sources’ groups are on the dispatcher. The driver writes one outcome per source to <TS>_consolidate.tsv, and when every source has one, carries on: the failed host keeps its finished groups (a source is deleted from only after all of it copied), so host_release keeps it, with consolidate failed at stage <stage> as the reason in kept_hosts.tsv. Its bucket adds no finish signal and is classed not consolidated, out of the recompute whatever the dispatcher’s log says, because a failure after the DELETE can leave log rows copied and streams not. The other hosts’ groups are recomputed and compared, and the run exits non-zero. Only when the outcomes are missing for some source (R died) does the driver exit right after consolidate, as before, with the --recompute-only recovery printed.

Before the copy the driver writes <TS>_consolidate_state.tsv (wsg, workspace, state, run_uid) with every source’s bucket in_flight, and rewrites it once each source has an outcome (ok, or failed:<stage>). A consolidate that dies mid-copy leaves the in_flight rows, so the record never reads as “nothing failed”. A bare --recompute-only names every group in a state other than ok and keeps it out of the recompute, because nothing on the dispatcher says whether its kept host was settled since; --wsgs= naming them is the operator’s word that it was. No record means the run never reached consolidate, so consolidate wrote nothing to the dispatcher.

Two things it does not do. It takes no lock, so do not run it while another driver on the same schema can resume: a driver paused with kill -STOP, as in #347’s recovery, would run a second barrier-view build and pool on the schema. And study_area_verify.sql stays red for a group whose failed attempt left an open log row on the dispatcher. That row is never closed, so verify reports the group as started and never finished, even after the re-run succeeds. In #246 the open rows were on the cloud hosts, so it did not show. Tests: tests/testthat/test-study_area_finish.R, on a scratch schema.

A runaway statement fails its group (link#371)

On 2026-10-23 OKAN sat 4 h in one statement (fresh’s near-river walk, CREATE TEMP TABLE pg_temp.frs_near_river_walk AS …), and the cloud hosts idled on it. The same statement on the same tables took 59 s afterwards, so the stall was neither the SQL nor the data. Nothing bounded a statement, and the operator found it in pg_stat_activity. Now each modelling statement is bounded, and one that runs past the bound fails its group like any other error, which the path above already handles.

  • The bound: --statement-timeout=<minutes>, default 30, 1 to 1440, with no unbounded mode. The driver sets it as PGOPTIONS='-c statement_timeout=<N>min' on both modelling legs: the local leg (after any PGOPTIONS the operator set) and the ssh command string (replacing the dispatcher’s, whose tuning is not the cyphers’). LNK_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MIN=<N> goes with it, and wsg_run_one.R refuses to model on a connection whose bound (from pg_settings, in ms; SHOW reads 60min as 1h) is any other, so a leg that lost PGOPTIONS fails its first group rather than running unbound. This is the both-legs rule LNK_GUARD_DOWNSTREAM and LNK_RUN_UID follow. libpq reads PGOPTIONS at connect, so the bound reaches every connection of the run and nothing else. The 2026-10-23 fix, ALTER ROLE postgres SET statement_timeout, reached every session on the host and had to be reset.
  • Why 30: the longest group that finished on 2026-10-23 took 16.3 min in total (SETN, then LNAR 13.8 and BULK 13.7; fresh_default.log), and no statement outlasts its group. Those are whole-group minutes from one run, and cyphers ran up to 2.9x the dispatcher’s time, so raise the bound when a top group is placed on a cypher by hand. A bound too tight costs one re-model and a --recompute-only; no bound cost four hours on 2026-10-23.
  • The recompute is not given it. wsg_recompute_one.R keeps its own SET statement_timeout = 10 min and lock_timeout = 1 min (§6). A session SET overrides PGOPTIONS either way, and the driver does not export it there.
  • What a host log shows: each group prints [wsg_run_one] <WSG> statement_timeout=30min. A cancelled statement prints [wsg_run_one] <WSG> TIMEOUT after 30min: <statement>, the SQL taken from the stack in a calling handler (.lnk_timeout_statement(); fresh’s bare dbExecute leaves it out of the error), or from .lnk_db_execute()’s Statement: when a transaction re-threw it. The downstream guard’s queries run under the same handler. Then the usual [WARN] … failed (continuing). The log row stays open with notes, as for any failed build.
  • What the summary shows: the group is in the “no rows” (or “earlier or partial”) class, and under it statement bound hit: lists each such group with its statement (run_timeouts, read from the run_uid’s <ts>_run_*.log, matched mid-line and byte-wise). Recover as above: the printed re-model carries the bound the run’s groups reported (read from those logs, so a --recompute-only session prints it too), then --recompute-only. A group still timing out on a re-model is a real slow statement: re-model it with a larger PGOPTIONS bound by hand, and look at pg_stat_activity while it runs.
  • Exercising it: LNK_TEST_STALL_WSG=<WSG> makes that group’s wsg_run_one.R run SELECT pg_sleep(3600) first. It works on the local leg only (it is not passed over ssh), and wsg_run_one.R refuses it when no bound is in effect. With --statement-timeout=1 the group fails after a minute, and the run carries on. The banner prints a TEST HOOK: line whenever the variable is set. Evidence: data-raw/logs/statement_timeout_371/.

Where a run’s time went: <TS>_phases.tsv (link#375)

Every speed number before this was rebuilt by hand from log tables, console logs and date_end columns. Now the driver writes one row per phase per host as the phase ends (data-raw/study_area_phases.sh), so a speed change is measured off a file, run after run (#377).

column holds
run_uid the run’s uid; under --recompute-only, the uid of the run it finishes
phase below
host dispatcher or a cypher workspace; blank for a run-wide phase
start_utc, end_utc ISO 8601, UTC
minutes end − start, one decimal
groups groups the phase covered; blank where it covers none
status ok, failed (errored, or left groups out), skipped (blank times)
  • The phases, in run order:
    • prep, run-wide: driver start to dispatch. It holds refresh, every cypher’s prep, both pre-flights and the bucket resolve.
    • prep, per cypher: from the spin to the end of its own prep. ok needs exit 0 and the === READY line the gate reads.
    • refresh: snapshot_bcfp.sh under --refresh-primitives; otherwise skipped.
    • model, per host: the leg, written by the leg’s own subshell when its loop ends. The driver waits on the legs one after another, so the moment a wait returns is not when that leg ended. The status is the session’s exit, which is 0 even when every group failed (each group soft-fails); account says whether the hosts finished.
    • account: per-host completeness from each database. failed when a host did not account for its bucket.
    • consolidate: the copy and the release that reads each source again; skipped with no cyphers.
    • burn: the explicit burn, not the EXIT trap’s. failed when a host it was free to burn is still up. A held host is the kept-hosts report’s to name.
    • coverage: failed when a run group has no rows from this run.
    • views: the log-table step and barriers_views_build.R.
    • recompute: the pool, ordering and judge included; skipped when views failed.
    • compare.
    • The tail is skipped when no group has rows.
  • Rows overlap, so never sum them. The run-wide prep holds refresh and every cypher’s prep, and the model legs run side by side. The summary prints the critical path, which is the first start to the last end, and the longest model leg.
  • A row per tracker cell. “Longest leg” is the longest model row. “Consolidate on the critical path” is the consolidate row, since it waits on every leg. “Recompute” is the recompute row. “Critical path” is the summary’s line. The phases.tsv sits beside the run’s other <TS>_* logs.
  • A run that dies keeps the rows it finished. The EXIT trap closes the phase it died in as failed and prints the table once. A kill does not stop a running leg, so that leg later writes its own row too. For one phase, host and start, the later row is the leg’s real end. Each leg’s wrapper is a subshell of the driver and carries its command line, so pkill -f study_area_run kills the wrappers as well. Their legs (wsg_run_one.R, the ssh session) run on, but write no later row. A phase a leg had already closed is not closed again. The file has every phase only on a run that reached its summary: a coverage FATAL, for one, leaves no tail rows.
  • --recompute-only writes its own <its TS>_phases.tsv, with a prep row for its preamble and then the tail. Its critical path covers that pass only. A path running from the original run through a hand re-model hours later would mean nothing.
  • --preflight-only writes no file.
  • Times come from one date -u call each, which prints both ISO and epoch. date is GNU on some hosts and BSD on others, so nothing parses a date with it, and the report parses ISO in perl. A date that fails costs only that row’s times.

Which host may be burned (link#347)

The count used to be [wsg_run_one] … done lines, anchored at line start. R writes warnings into the same stream, and one flushed without a newline put the marker mid-line (… :[wsg_run_one] FIRE done in 4.6 min), so run 20261017_004619-3f4c713b hid 18 finished groups, consolidated only what it counted, and would have burned the hosts holding the rest. The rules now, all in data-raw/study_area_hosts.sh:

  • The database counts, the log only adds. consolidate takes database ∪ log done. The log cannot be the count (mid-line markers), and the database alone can undercount: .lnk_log_run_finish() is a soft UPDATE after persist, and a lost LNK_RUN_UID leaves every row’s run_uid NULL. Both probes are framed by sentinels, because ssh can exit 0 whatever the remote command did; no sentinels means unknown, never “nothing”.
  • A cypher is held from dispatch. It is released only when its dispatch session exited 0 and, after consolidate, its database holds no finished group: one with <persist>.streams rows left that this run finished there by any signal (database, log done, or streams_mapping_code rows, which within a run only the final persist writes). schema_consolidate deletes what it copied from the source, so what is left was not consolidated: measured, not assumed. A group with streams rows and no other signal is partial (it failed after the pre-persist, R/lnk_pipeline_run.R:240); it does not hold the host and is never consolidated.
  • Provenance and settledness are checked, not assumed. A cypher spins from a warm image and lnk_persist_init keeps rows, so before dispatch the driver records which of each bucket already have streams or streams_mapping_code rows (host_baseline); their mapping-code rows are not this run’s, and such a group with no finish signal of this run is groups_unknown, never partial. With no baseline, mapping-code rows count as groups_unknown too. Unknown groups hold the host and are never recovered. After dispatch the driver writes to a cypher in exactly two ways, the dispatch ssh session and schema_consolidate (which copies, then deletes from the source). A killed driver runs its EXIT trap while either keeps going, so a host is unsettled unless its session ended 0 (host_wait records the status only once wait returns) and consolidate is not in flight (CONSOLIDATING). An unsettled host’s groups are “not finished when probed”, never “partial”, and the record says to re-measure. A report from the trap reads the host’s log row and run log itself when accounting never ran.
  • A held host is kept on every exit path, abort included, and so is a host whose burn did not complete. Each is a row in <TS>_kept_hosts.tsv (reason, run_uid, schema, groups, whether those groups were measured, the command that prints its address, the command that burns it), the banner prints from the EXIT trap, and the run exits non-zero. --keep-cyphers alone is not a failure; a host it keeps that is also held for cause is.
  • A host whose database did not answer is left out of consolidate: the same route would fail there and take the other hosts’ consolidate with it.
  • Pre-flight fails on a cypher already up in this run’s workspaces: that is most likely a host an earlier run kept, and cypher_up would adopt it. Others warn, except the long-lived default cypher.

To recover a kept host: run its ip_command, consolidate its groups with schema_consolidate(schema = <schema>, sources = list(list(host = "cypher@<ip>", via = "docker", bucket = c(...)))), then run its burn_command. Only groups, never groups_partial or groups_unknown, and only where groups_measured is yes: groups is then the finished work still on the host. unsettled means wait until nothing runs there and re-measure. schema_consolidate deletes its bucket on the dispatcher before it copies, so consolidating a group the host holds only in part loses the dispatcher’s copy of its persist rows (its log rows survive, link#354). Where both sides have a log table, consolidate refuses a source outright (stage = "dest_log_newer", nothing deleted) when a group has a log row on the dispatcher and the source’s newest is older or absent: the persist tables carry no run id, so that newest row is what says which build they hold. So a group the host no longer holds at all (already consolidated, then deleted from the source, log rows included) is refused rather than lost, and a group re-run on the dispatcher during recovery is never overwritten by the kept host’s older build. A group with persist rows but no log row on the dispatcher (built before the log tables, link#127: 59 of fresh’s 98 groups, 0 in fresh_default, 2026-10-17) is not protected: it is deleted and, if the host no longer holds it, not replaced. Where it says no, find out what is left first. If the run’s recompute ran, it ran without the kept groups: recompute each one and each run group upstream of it (wsg_recompute_one.R). If it did not run (consolidate recorded no outcome for some source, or no run group had rows from this run), recompute every group of the run; the banner says which. A missing <schema>.streams or streams_mapping_code on a host reads as unknown, not empty: every dispatched cypher has both. Tests: tests/testthat/test-study_area_hosts.R runs the lib in bash with stubbed ssh, psql, tofu and doctl.

Host buckets are derived, not chosen

data-raw/study_area_buckets.R partitions the focal set into drainage-independent components by union-find over per-WSG frs_wsg_drainage() closures, then LPT-packs the components onto hosts and writes research/study_areas.md. Overlapping closures would make consolidate last-writer-wins on the shared WSGs, so the script asserts disjointness. Never partition by wscode_ltree root — see §8b.

The atom can be a single group (link#361). The component rule was written for access at model time. Since link#175 the post-consolidate recompute settles access, mapping code and (link#349) the gated habitat flags from every group’s persisted barriers, and the driver models both legs with LNK_GUARD_DOWNSTREAM=warn and LNK_HABITAT_GATE=0. The split test of 2026-10-23 modelled the Peace’s 26 groups on two hosts in the worst order and found nothing the order can reach that differs from the one-host build (data-raw/logs/provincial_361/split_verdict.md: the 55 of 442 differing digests are cross-host arithmetic of at most 3.7e-9 m and the test’s own 26-group scope). So study_area_buckets.R --atom=group packs single modelable groups, which lets modelling finish before the largest component would (the Fraser: 205 of 873 host-minutes on the 2026-10-17 minutes, 231 of 1,077 on 2026-10-23’s), and prints the makespan under both atoms. Its --focal= strings are each host’s exact list in the global downstream-first order, and the run takes them with study_area_run.sh --buckets-exact (study_area_wsgs.R --exact: no closure expansion, the species filter only, order kept). In exact mode an overlap between hosts’ lists is fatal, the banner says buckets: exact, and <TS>_run_wsgs.tsv carries bucket_mode. Keep component atoms when fewer guard warnings at open matter more than minutes; at four hosts the two atoms tie on this run’s minutes, and group atoms pay from five hosts on. Two cautions from the test: a build is byte-identical on one host and differs by up to 3.7e-9 m across architectures, so “identical across hosts” is a digest after rounding; and a recompute over a subset of groups differs from the full one wherever a group holds lines coded to another basin or with barriers below it in a group outside the subset (NATR’s two Fraser-coded segments; TOOD’s two with barriers below them in FROG, LKEC, UKEC and ULRD).

8. Fast verification recipes

# What does bcfp emit for a WSG's mapping_code (local snapshot, no tunnel)?
docker exec fresh-db psql -U postgres -d fwapg -c \
  "SELECT mapping_code_bt, count(*) FROM fresh.streams_vw_bcfp
   WHERE watershed_group_code='PARS' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;"

# What does link emit (after a mapping_code=TRUE run)?
docker exec fresh-db psql -U postgres -d fwapg -c \
  "SELECT mapping_code_bt, count(*) FROM fresh_default.streams_mapping_code
   WHERE watershed_group_code='PARS' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;"

# Inspect a barrier view's shape / blocks_species
docker exec fresh-db psql -U postgres -d fwapg -c \
  "SELECT pg_get_viewdef('fresh_default.barriers_bt_unified', true);"

# Single-WSG tunnel-free build (the headline path)
bash data-raw/wsgs_run_m4_offline.sh --wsgs=PARS --config=default \
  --schema=fresh_default --force --mapping-code

Local docker fwapg: host=localhost port=5432 dbname=fwapg user=postgres password=postgres (compose at ~/Projects/repo/fresh/docker/).
